stage: Optional non-consuming TLS stream retirement, prerequisite candidate for framed RPC TLS

contract.predicate: terminal TLS + actual caller-only TLS references, then public physical TCP retirement
contract.poll_allocator_scope: No XRT allocations; exact ambient error preserved on OK/TIMEOUT
contract.wait: Reject every same-Engine Worker, including timeout 0; one remaining monotonic timeout across both layers
contract.waiters: Concurrent external waiters with stable sole caller owner
contract.actions: Does not consume, close, cancel, drive IO, destroy or release the owner
contract.resources: Retired caller-owned sessions can still hold pooled buffers. Destroy TLS owners before requiring Engine resource teardown; keep destructor code/data resident through Destroy; Engine and external callers join separately before unload.
contract.ownership_graph: Count/Trace/Busy policies are not used as lifecycle predicates.

implementation.optional_storage: One mutex and condition per TLS stream; actual target sizeof measured below
implementation.release: References above two use load/CAS fast decrement. Transitions to caller-only and final destruction are serialized under retirement mutex; notify all waiters before publication. No stream access after successful fast decrement.
implementation.feature_off: Original TLS storage and release body retained; no new feature branch/storage/synchronization when unselected.
implementation.cold_costs: One mutex and condition initialization/unit per stream when selected; native OS synchronization allocation is not quantified by the XRT heap counter.
implementation.composition_note: Existing extensions may compose owned context lifetimes with native TCP retirement. This optional public leaf adds a non-consuming TLS barrier; existing extension module dependencies are not forced to select it.
